headline: GOLD SMASHES $4,100 FLOOR, SILVER DIVES 6% TO $55 — SEPTEMBER CPI SHOCKER REVIVES RATE HIKE ODDS
snippet: Spot gold fell to $4,098.80 (-$61.30, -1.47%) on October 14 — breaching key $4,100 technical support — while silver cratered 6.16% to $55.41, as September CPI came in at 3.7% vs. the 3.6% consensus. The CME FedWatch tool placed odds of an October 27-28 rate hike at 41.5%; first gold support sits at $4,072.70. The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, its worst session since July.

headline: ALUMINIUM SINKS BELOW $3,000 FOR FIRST TIME SINCE DECEMBER — BASE METALS CRACK UNDER RATE HIKE PRESSURE
snippet: LME aluminium fell to US$2,978 per tonne on October 14, its lowest since December 31, 2025, as emerging oversupply signals and rising US rate-hike expectations hit industrial metals. Copper retreated to $14,484 after earlier touching a three-week high on Escondida-driven supply fears. Both metals face continued pressure ahead of the October 27-28 Fed meeting.

headline: PAN GLOBAL HITS 7.29 g/t Au OVER 9M IN SPAIN — CÁRMENES DISCOVERY EXPANDING IN ALL DIRECTIONS
snippet: Pan Global Resources (TSXV: PGZ) extended its Providencia gold discovery at the Cármenes Project in northern Spain with highlights of 7.29 g/t Au over 9 metres and 1.53 g/t Au over 38 metres from 19 completed drillholes. Mineralization remains open in multiple directions and at depth across the rapidly expanding near-surface gold system, setting the stage for a first resource estimate.

headline: BRIXTON METALS WRAPS CAMP CREEK 2026 — BEST HOLE 17.58M AT 1.47 g/t AuEq AS RESOURCE ESTIMATE BEGINS
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSXV: BBB) completed its 15-hole 2026 drill campaign at the Camp Creek high-sulphidation target at the Thorn Gold Project in British Columbia. Top hole THN26-385 returned 17.58 metres at 1.47 g/t AuEq from 135.52 metres depth, and THN26-371 hit 58 metres at 0.50 g/t AuEq. APEX Geoscience has commenced a Mineral Resource Estimate, with results expected in Q1 2027.

headline: DE-DOLLARIZATION IN REAL TIME — WHY CHINA KEEPS STACKING GOLD EVEN AS PRICES SLIDE FROM RECORDS
snippet: Mike Maharrey of Money Metals Exchange examines why China continues driving record gold imports despite bullion retreating roughly $1,500 from its January all-time high. The analysis traces Beijing's strategy to reduce dollar reserve exposure, citing record CNBC-tracked Chinese gold inflows and an ongoing geopolitical realignment that makes gold Beijing's preferred reserve alternative as US monetary policy tightens.

headline: GOLD'S AUTUMN DIP IS A SEASONAL SETUP, NOT A BREAKDOWN — HAMILTON MAPS THE WINTER BUY ZONE
snippet: Adam Hamilton of Zeal Research argues at GoldSeek that gold's October selloff follows a well-documented seasonal pattern where the metal typically weakens in late September before rallying sharply into year-end. Historical data from multiple bull markets shows the autumn pullback often precedes the strongest quarter, making the current $4,072-$4,100 support zone a high-probability accumulation range for patient junior mining investors.

headline: MI6 MINERALS 260: GRADE CONTROL DRILLING BACKS 6.2Moz BULLABULLING RESOURCE — NEW GOLD BELOW PIT SHELL
snippet: Minerals 260 (ASX: MI6) reported that 320 grade control holes and 53 infill/extensional holes at the Bullabulling Gold Project in Western Australia returned grades consistent with the existing 6.2Moz resource model. Critically, extensional holes found gold mineralization approximately 100 metres below the Phoenix pit shell, opening meaningful resource upside ahead of the planned feasibility study.

headline: ASX GOLD AND COPPER MINERS OPEN SHARPLY LOWER — US CPI + OIL AT $106 RESET RATE EXPECTATIONS
snippet: Australian gold and mining stocks fell at the October 15 open after hot US September CPI data reignited rate hike fears and sent the S&P 500 down 1.1% — its worst session since July. Brent crude surging to $106.06 per barrel added a separate cost-push inflation concern for mining operations, with BHP and Rio Tinto both retreating and gold futures easing further in early Sydney trading.

headline: COPPER AND ALUMINIUM BOTH CRACK ON RATE FEAR RETURN — BASE METALS GIVE BACK ESCONDIDA GAINS
snippet: Following September CPI at 3.7%, base metals surrendered their Escondida-driven gains on October 14, with copper falling 0.6% to $14,484 and aluminium breaking multi-month support to dip below $3,000. The analysis covers how rising rate expectations hit industrial metals through two channels: higher borrowing costs and slower growth projections — both directly relevant to junior copper and battery metals valuations.
